title: Throughput Canary: Time-windowed limiter + drift-detection for automated batch/cache tuning
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Goal: Build a conservative, observable canary that applies batching/cache configuration deltas in small, time-windowed steps and uses drift-detection on latency/throughput/KV-cache-miss signals to automatically throttle, route, or roll back changes. This ticket implements the core limiter + drift detector and the rollout orchestration hooks (apply, monitor, step-up/step-down, rollback triggers).

Background: We already have offline recommendations for batching and prefix caching. Past incidents show microburst traffic and unexpected KV cache churn can cause transient latency regressions if config changes are applied too aggressively. This feature aims to automate safe application of recommenders while ensuring SLOs are preserved.

Design highlights:
- Time-windowed limiter: apply config changes in small increments over N windows (default N=6, window=30s) with a maximum change per window (e.g., batch_size +1 or cache_ttl *1.1).
- Burst score metric: combine short-term latency (P95), call success rate, throughput delta, and kv_cache_miss_rate into a single bounded score (0.0-1.0). Score > 0.6 triggers conservative action.
- Drift-detection: lightweight, non-parametric test using rolling quantiles + EWMA to detect sudden shifts vs expected distribution. Two-mode detection: synthetic canary baseline + live-traffic comparison to guard against seasonal shifts.
- SLO-aware routing: when score borderline, route a configurable percentage of traffic to a fallback runtime/model variant with conservative parameters.
- Safe rollback: explicit rollback triggers when score crosses hard threshold for M consecutive windows or cumulative cost of violation exceeds budget. Rollback is multi-stage: step-down, pause, full revert.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Limiter can apply a recommended batch/cache delta across traffic pools without manual intervention in staging.
2) Drift detector identifies injected latency/kv-cache regressions within 2 windows in staging tests.
3) SLO-aware routing reduces affected traffic to <20% and keeps P95 within target for primary pool 95% of the time during a simulated regression.
4) End-to-end e2e test, PR, and dashboard links provided; runbook updated.

Non-goals: global re-architecture of the recommender, full ML-based anomaly detection (this ticket intentionally uses lightweight statistics).
comments: 2026-02-20 — Alex Chen: Drafted initial spec after postmortem with infra and reliability teams. Key risk: KV-cache churn not captured by current telemetry. Proposed adding kv_cache_miss_rate metric to burst score.

2026-02-24 — Priya Nair: Reviewed spec; suggested default conservative parameters (N=6 windows, window=30s) and adding synthetic canary traffic to baseline the drift detector. Assigning ENG infra for telemetry hooks.

2026-03-02 — Engineering: Implemented prototype limiter in runtime branch 'throughput-canary/prototype'. Added metrics: canary_burst_score, canary_drift_p95_diff, canary_kv_miss_rate. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12861

2026-03-04 — Reliability review (Miguel Torres): Feedback: use quantile-summary sketches for p95 delta to reduce memory; ensure EWMA timescale configurable per route. Added follow-up task to add memory budget guard.

2026-03-06 — QA (Sofia Patel): Wrote staged fault-injection scenarios: 1) KV-cache eviction storm, 2) synthetic latency injection, 3) traffic microburst with concurrency spike. Observed drift detector detected 2/3 scenarios within 1 window; KV storm needed tweak to detection sensitivity.

2026-03-08 — Priya Nair: Updated rollout policy: add 'route-recovery' step when fallback has lower cost impact but stable SLOs. Updated runbook draft at Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Throughput+Canary+Design

2026-03-10 — Alex Chen: Integration tests passing in staging. Created Grafana dashboard for canary metrics: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/throughput_canary/overview. Preparing canary for limited production trial on dev-customer pool next week.
